analysis: Reviewed scripts/test-provider-release-publication.py (head lines 1-395). The change is test-only. It adds create_tag_repository (lines 19-31) and a ReleaseChangelog test class (34-70). It also changes the tag-annotation retention test (275-305) to use real local git tags and checks that annotation text is preserved verbatim. The text is treated as data (a marker file must not be created via $(touch ...)), and signature armor is stripped. Security-relevant observations: the git fixture isolates itself from machine-wide config (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, core.hooksPath=/dev/null, signing disabled, GIT_DIR/WORK_TREE stripped). Temp directories are used, with no network and no credentials. The fixture uses fake release key 'never-log' only. Existing tests keep covering the release-publication gates relevant to A-011/A-017/TB-011/T-054. These include tag/master withdrawal blocking registration, digest mismatch failing before I/O, require_app_attest_qualification being enforced, and registration preceding alias advancement. No production code is changed in this unit, so no control is weakened. Remaining question for integration: the actual release_changelog implementation in scripts/provider-release-publication.py is outside this batch. Whether it invokes git with a shell or argument injection from the tag name, and whether it handles untrusted annotation text safely when it is placed into release notes or the payload, should be verified there. The tests only assert the expected behavior.
